reasons: v0 has the best raw coverage (60 tokens with 2+ usable items) but fails the top rubric criterion: the Sherlock address item uses 12 Grimmauld Place and 4 Privet Drive as distractors, the Sirius constellation/Dog Star items and the Remus she-wolf item favour fans, and the Grindelwald and Rowena items name concept characters; it also has absurd distractors (Draco hemisphere, community service) and several non-essential-token items (Farley Granger/Strangers on a Train, Hermione/Menelaus, Exit pursued by a bear). v1 removes those neutrality leaks but keeps others (Bloomsbury -> London, Draco named after a dragon, Hermione/Winter's Tale, Umbrage) and introduces many forced capitalised or quoted words (Grin and bear it, Road Hog, Quirky, Riddle me this, gee-wiz, "Potter wasp"), plus giveaway clues (Mrs Dalloway, General Theory, J.R. Ewing, Allan Quatermain, Cameron Diaz cast). v2 fixes essentially all of these: the clue-carrying items were rewritten so the token carries the item, the forced items were removed or rephrased, the Draco=dragon and Bloomsbury=London items are gone, and distractors are same-type and plausible. Its cost is coverage: 54 tokens with 2+ usable items versus 58/60, from reclassifying ' Grin', ' Hermione' and 'Hermione' as exclusive and cutting 'Potter', ' Riddle' and 'wiz' to 1-2 items. I think those reclassifications are defensible: the capitalised ' Grin' has only obscure or forced outside uses, and the outside Hermiones are either obscure or fan trivia. base_acc is essentially the same for all three (0.910-0.912). Neutrality and token essentiality come before coverage in the rubric, so v2 is the best set, and the 4-6 tokens it loses are a cheaper price than v0's fan-advantage items. Only two v2 items still look clearly flawed.
residual_problems: Terry Pratchett's novel Hogfather is a parody of which holiday figure?: answer given away by the word 'father' in Hogfather (Father Christmas), so the token is not essential
In Snow White, the queen disguised as a witch gives Snow White a poisoned what?: distractor 'Comb' is also a poisoned gift in the Grimm tale, so two options can be correct
